title: Normalize table row collapse behavior and tokenized spacing for data tables
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background:
Across multiple products we observed inconsistent collapsing behavior for dense data tables: some rows collapse with animation but shift inner content unpredictably; auto-layout gaps are reused inconsistently (px tokens used directly), and interactive states (hover/focus/pressed) are implemented as overrides on leaf instances which causes a combinatorial variant explosion. This creates maintenance burden, visual regressions across breakpoints, and accessibility/hit-area regressions on touch.

Goals:
- Establish a canonical variant axis for table rows (state: default / collapsed / expanded / selected) and decouple interactive overlays from core row content.
- Replace ad-hoc pixel spacing with semantic, tokenized spacing (table-row-gap-compact, table-row-gap-regular, table-row-padding-x).
- Normalize autolayout constraints so row height is driven by padding tokens and a single content-size constraint (min/max) rather than manual frame resizing.
- Provide a migration plan and Figma publish preflight checks to prevent regressions.

Proposed solution overview:
1) Variant model: decompose row into 3 layers in the master component — background layer, content layer (layout for columns/cells), and interaction overlay. Introduce a single variant axis `row_state` with values: `default`, `collapsed`, `expanded`, `selected`. Interaction overlay will be a separate optional variant/instance that references a small overlay component for hover/focus/press visuals and hit target expansion.
2) Tokens: add new semantic spacing tokens scoped to tables: `table.row.padding-y.compact`, `table.row.padding-y.regular`, `table.cell.gap-x.small`, `table.cell.gap-x.large`. Update token documentation and migration mapping from legacy px tokens.
3) Auto-layout rules: set row frame to vertical auto-layout with fixed padding (from tokens) and content hugging set to 'fill container' for primary cells. Enforce column cell constraints with explicit min-width tokens where appropriate.
4) Publish flow: add a pre-publish checklist in the Figma file with checks that fail if any instance overrides padding or contains deprecated tokens. Export a small CSV of instances needing manual migration.
5) Rollout: pilot with `payments` and `admin-console` teams, validate telemetry for visual regressions, and ship to the global library once pilot signoff complete.

Why this is different from past work:
Instead of pruning variants piecemeal, this work enforces an explicit separation of concerns (visual/content/interaction) and introduces table-specific semantic tokens. That reduces variant combinatorics and makes future layout tweaks lower risk.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: large number of existing instances that will break on publish. Mitigation: automatic instance scanner + migration CSV + two-week pilot with manual QA.
- Risk: developers rely on legacy px tokens in code. Mitigation: include mapping table in token spec and provide migration notes for frontend.

Consequences for engineering:
- Frontend will need updated token names and a small CSS mapping layer change. ENG ticket ENG-19834 coordinates the runtime mapping.

Next steps:
- Complete Figma masters and token updates (design).
- Run instance inventory script and produce migration CSV (design + tooling).
- Open PR with token rename and update example table components in the design kit (frontend).

Acceptance criteria:
acceptance_criteria: Master row component exposes a single row_state axis with 4 values and three distinct layers (background/content/interaction)
All table spacing uses new semantic tokens and no new instances use deprecated px tokens
Autolayout constraints: row height is controlled by padding tokens and content-size; no manual height overrides remain on master instances
Pre-publish checklist runs and lists zero blocking violations for pilot teams; CSV of remaining deprecated instances is generated
Pilot teams (payments, admin-console) confirm visual parity and accessibility checks pass (focus order, 44px minimum interactive target where required)
